review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that students have the best achievement should be rewarded, whereas others believe it would make students improving themselves. Personally, I am strongly believe that both of students offer reward.

Admittedly, parents and school, reward to students show the best academic results is correct. Students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they can deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, which helps towards overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition to be seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Allowing students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition and thus enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, I believe that students have improve in learning also reward. Firstly, only a few smart students can come first and receive the reward cause others to think that their effort is futile, this is primarily because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. This can lead students prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Secondly, emphasizing improvements encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that both of kind student effort should be reward.

paragraphs: Opinions are divided over whether schools should reward students who achieve the best academic results or give greater recognition to students who make progress. I strongly believe that both groups should receive rewards.

Admittedly, rewarding students who achieve the best academic results is justified. Students who have diligently applied themselves to their studies deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win rewards, which may lead to overall academic gains. Furthermore, competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students become used to this reality and can thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, other students may feel that further effort is futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Secondly, emphasizing improvements encourages all students to be diligent in their studies and helps them understand that they need to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. The constant desire to outdo themselves may benefit students more than the determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that both students who achieve the best academic results and those who make progress should be rewarded.

Admittedly, technology bring a useful cultural and historical experience. Those cannot afford and have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries is still essential. Firstly, online experience which cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary in the future as people can view historical objects and works of art on a computer. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, technology brings a useful cultural and historical experience. This is predicated on the assumption that high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. For example, a museum can allow people to explore ancient artefacts and artworks online, making it possible for visitors to see these objects without visiting the museum. People who cannot afford a museum visit or have mobility issues can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are still essential. Firstly, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Seeing an artefact in person evokes emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For instance, seeing a deceased person's clothes displayed in a museum can give visitors a more realistic sense of the past. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs and symbolize the identity of a region. It naturally follows that museums and galleries attract tourists and facilitate bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although technology has developed, direct experience in public museums and art galleries remains necessary.

Admittedly, one might argue that should be prohibited because even a minor error can death of participant, a example is skydiving. Futhermore, this is a unrealistic, a police officer follows every individuals just prevent them participating in dangerous sports. As a result, a prohibition exist only a paper, worse, it could drive practice underground making it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

However, I strongly believe that people be permitted to do any sports, as long as they understand risks receive sufficient training. For example, people want to play deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping should join reputable club which appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Secondly, beginners should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accident occur. This, they can recognise dangers and respond appropriately. paragraphs: There is an opinion that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, whereas others believe individuals should be free to take part in any sport or activity they want. Personally, I am of the latter school of thought, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited. This is because even a minor error can cause a participant's death; an example is skydiving. However, a ban is not feasible. This is because these sports take place in remote locations, such as mountain cliffs, where surveillance and control are minimal. Furthermore, it is unrealistic to expect an officer to follow every individual just to prevent them from participating in dangerous sports. As a result, a ban may exist only on paper and may drive the practice underground, making basic safety standards harder to ensure.

Instead, I strongly believe that people should be permitted to do any sport as long as they understand the risks and receive sufficient training. For example, people who want to try deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping should join a reputable club with appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. In addition, beginners should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur. This training helps them recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Thus, proper training and necessary precautions make participation safer, although no activity is entirely risk-free.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that banning dangerous sports is neither practical nor effective. Freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that children should learn through trial and error, whereas other people believe that adults should help them avoid mistakes. Personally, I strongly believe that children's freedom to make mistakes should be encouraged, provided that the errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of a trial-and-error approach often emphasise that many mistakes can be prevented. Firstly, many mistakes are avoidable. For example, children need not get hurt by knives, fire or electricity to learn to be careful. Secondly, parents should shield children from harm and forestall mistakes to fulfil this duty. Finally, adults who pre-emptively help children can enjoy peace of mind, since they have done their best to protect and raise their child.

However, those who favour children's freedom to make mistakes have their own valid reasoning. Parents cannot be around all the time; consequently, children will have to experiment with new things, making some mistakes inevitable. Furthermore, from these experiences, they can learn invaluable lessons that stand them in good stead later in life. In addition, if children are shielded from everything, they may grow up overdependent on others, an undesirable trait.

Overall, it seems to me that parents should allow children to learn from mistakes to prepare for the future, provided that parents have to intervene or give guidance on important matters. Such guidance helps prevent errors that may derail their future.

task.text:
Some people think children have the freedom to make mistakes, while other people believe that adults should prevent children from making mistakes.
Discuss both views and give your opinions.
